standard_prerequisites: The derived descent tower situation with its system of pseudo-coherent objects K_n and the limit object K defined as the derived limit in the quasi-coherent derived category
The derived categories of spaces lemma that the direct image computing the stages of a pseudo-coherent system is pseudo-coherent with formation commuting with base change
The More on Algebra lemma that a derived limit of pseudo-coherent objects with compatible base change data is pseudo-coherent and recovers the stages on base change
The exact functor RGamma on the quasi-coherent derived category commuting with products and hence with derived limits
core_obligations: Set up the stages M_n = RGamma(X_n, K_n tensor E_n); by the derived categories of spaces lemma each M_n is a pseudo-coherent object of D(A_n) whose formation commutes with base change, so the transition maps M_n tensor A_{n-1} -> M_{n-1} coming from the thickenings are isomorphisms
The More on Algebra limit lemma makes R lim M_n a pseudo-coherent object of D(A) whose base change to A_n recovers M_n

The exact functor RGamma(X, -) commutes with products and hence with derived limits, giving the chain RGamma(X, E tensor K) = R lim RGamma(X, E tensor K_n) = R lim RGamma(X_n, E_n tensor K_n) = R lim M_n
proof_roadmap: Produce the stages with base change compatible pseudo-coherence
Pass to the derived limit with the algebra limit lemma for pseudo-coherent objects
Chain the limit commutation of RGamma against the definition of K
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is the pseudo-coherence of M = RGamma(X, K tensor E) and its base change compatibility along the derived descent tower at source lines 2752-2765, label lemma-compute-against-perfect-derived, whose proof occupies source lines 2767-2791. The proof is not a bare citation chain: it sets up the stages M_n, derives their base change compatible pseudo-coherence, passes to the limit object with recovery isomorphisms, and carries out the commutation argument that RGamma(X, -) commutes with products and hence with derived limits, chaining it against the definition of K as the derived limit of the system. The counted statement records none of this.
